description: Every scenario the sample apps offer. One build, N scenarios: the drawer switches at runtime so a matrix that used to need N rebuilds needs N taps. All four apps must implement every id.

scenarios.label: Normal
scenarios.description: Happy path with valid sandbox credentials.

scenarios.label: Expired token
scenarios.description: Auth token is structurally valid but already expired, so the SDK must refresh before it can submit.
scenarios.forces: A well-formed JWT whose exp is in the past. Structural validity matters: a garbage string tests parsing, not refresh.

scenarios.label: Refresh fails
scenarios.description: The refresh callback returns an unusable token, so the failure path must surface rather than retry forever.
scenarios.forces: Refresh callback resolves with an expired or malformed token.

scenarios.label: No result callback
scenarios.description: Host provides no result callback. The SDK must not crash or hang.

scenarios.label: Throwing callback
scenarios.description: Host callback throws. The exception must not corrupt SDK state or take the app down.

scenarios.label: Offline then retry
scenarios.description: Submission starts with no connectivity, then connectivity returns.
scenarios.forces: Airplane mode or a blocked host during submission; restored afterwards.

scenarios.label: Brand default
scenarios.description: Ship state: Smile ID branding, light or dark per the Settings APPEARANCE switch.

scenarios.label: Clashing host
scenarios.description: A deliberately distant host theme — different seed colour, corner radius and typeface — applied through the SDK's public theme override. Exposes host-versus-SDK styling collisions that a brand-matched default hides.
scenarios.forces: Theme override with values far from the SDK defaults.
scenarios.surface: launch argument / debug drawer only — NOT a Settings row, because the design has no such control

scenarios.label: Partner override
scenarios.description: A plausible partner palette through the same public override, asserting which tokens follow the override and which stay SDK-owned.
scenarios.forces: Theme override with a realistic partner palette.
scenarios.surface: launch argument / debug drawer only — NOT a Settings row, because the design has no such control

notes: flow scenarios are selectable together with an entry route (see launch-args.json 'route'); theme scenarios apply on top of any flow scenario.
Every scenario must be reachable from the drawer AND from a launch argument, because automation cannot rely on tapping through a drawer reliably on every platform.
'forces' documents the mechanism so the four implementations force the same condition the same way; keep it factual, not prescriptive about code.

Theme scenarios reconciled with the design 2026-08-12: the design's Settings screen exposes only a Dark mode switch, so brandDefault is the shipped control and clashingHost/partnerOverride stay automation-only (launch arg or debug drawer). If they should become visible controls later, they become Settings rows under APPEARANCE — that is the customization surface the design already implies.
Flow scenarios compose with products: `scenario` says how the environment misbehaves, `autostart` says which product to launch. Every flow scenario must be reachable for every capture product.

products.comment: What the products grid offers, in design order. `jobType` is the SDK enum name; test ids derive from `id`. `label` is the SDK's job-type name in full and is what the verifications row and the result card read. `cardTitle` + `cardFamily` are the product CARD's two runs, added 2026-08-25 from node 5487:1351 — the card shortens the title to fit a 114.5dp text column and puts the family on a second line. They are specified here rather than derived because four platforms must abbreviate identically: 'Enhanced Doc.' and 'Enh. Doc' are both reasonable and only one is right. The 2026-08-13 ruling that `label` is the job-type name in full still holds.

items.label: Enhanced KYC
items.note: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13: added to fill the grid's empty slot. No camera step — the SDK flow composes consent() + processing() only, which needs no SDK change and makes this the one journey proving the flow works without capture(). Needs a 6th product card designed (icon + hue).

notInDesign.comment: BVN is the only SDK job type left out. iOS `buildJobRequest()` documents it as NOT SUPPORTED and throws, so excluding it is correct rather than a gap.

products.flowOrder: product tapped → Consent Details Form (sample-owned user details, seeded from the active profile — the design labels these fields 'ATTACHED TO EVERY JOB', so every product shows it) → ID details form (sample-owned, only when needsIdDetails) → SDK flow [consent → instructions → capture → preview → processing] → verification details in the processing state. Everything before the SDK flow is sample-owned, which is why no SDK change is needed.
products.flowOrderRuling: OWNER RULING 2026-08-13: e.g. SmartSelfie Enrollment → Consent Details Form → SDK flow. The Figma prototype still shows the SDK consent screen first; that wiring is stale and is not being updated.
products.needsUserDetailsNote: Set true for every product on the evidence of the design's own label 'USER DETAILS — ATTACHED TO EVERY JOB' (board 06 profile config) plus the owner's SmartSelfie Enrollment example.
products.captureless: Products with capture=false (enhancedKyc) compose the SDK flow WITHOUT capture() or preview(): consent() + processing(). Everything before the SDK flow is unchanged.
products.sectionRename: 'Authentication' -> 'Biometric Authentication' 2026-08-25, per node 5487:1364. The section KEY in each app's enum is unchanged; only the displayed label moved.
